title: "IMSE 456/656 — Project Management"
subtitle: "Fall 2026 · North Dakota State University"

Project management taught the way it is actually practiced now: the quantitative core
(WBS, CPM, PERT, EVM) alongside adaptive delivery (Scrum, Kanban, flow), with hybrid
treated as the default real-world case rather than a compromise — and with an AI layer
running through every week, because the artifacts of this discipline are increasingly
drafted by machines and audited by people.

## What you will be able to do

1. Decide **which delivery approach fits a given project** and defend the choice against a specific alternative.
2. Build and interpret the **core quantitative artifacts**: WBS, CPM network, PERT distribution, crash analysis, EVM report.
3. Run the **adaptive artifacts**: product backlog, sprint mechanics, cumulative flow, Little's Law.
4. **Read the evidence critically** — distinguish a base rate from a vendor statistic, and name what a project-success number is actually measuring.
5. Diagnose a failing project and propose interventions ranked by expected effect, not by convention.
6. **Specify, build, and govern an AI agent** that maintains a live project artifact — and say what it got wrong.

## Textbook

Larson &amp; Gray, *Project Management: The Managerial Process* (2024 Release), McGraw Hill — **optional**.
Chapter readings are listed each week. Everything you are assessed on is in the lecture notes on this site.
